MUSIC VIDEO OCTOBER 2026 · 2:32

Pumpkin Leash.

A Halloween night in New York, starring my dog Archie. I wrote the words, then made the song, the storyboard, the animation and the edit.

59 shots20 animated clips112 BPM$4.93 of generation

One night, told from the other end of the leash.

The lyrics follow a single Halloween night. Archie gets into his bat wings and cape at the door, the two of us haunt the block, and every chorus breaks into a run through the city. The bridge slows down at a red light, and the night ends with him asleep on the candy bag.

Every shot in the video comes from a line of the song. The cut ends on real photos of Archie, which is the part that matters most to me.

How it was made

05 STEPS
  1. SONG

    Words first

    I wrote the lyrics, then made the track with Suno as playful, spooky synth-pop at 112 BPM. A speech-recognition pass gave every word a timestamp, so the on-screen lyrics land exactly on the vocal.

    Suno · Whisper
  2. CASTING

    Getting Archie right

    The first stylized design was a generic cartoon puppy with perky ears and big eyes. It didn't look like him. The second round was built only from his recent photos, with the things that make him Archie written in: lanky legs, a wiry white coat, a ginger head, long shaggy ears and a messy fringe.

    FLUX.2 klein · reference images
  3. STORYBOARD

    59 shots, one per line

    Each lyric became a shot with its own keyframe: the bowl of bones, the moon over the water towers, the skeletons on the fire escape, the red light. I checked every frame against his photos and redid the ones that drifted.

    Runware · about half a cent a frame
  4. MOTION

    Animating the big moments

    Twenty keyframes became six-second animated clips: the runs, the leaf jump, the bark into the lens, the block party. The rest are stills with camera moves. One clip turned Archie into a different dog halfway through, so it was re-rolled.

    MiniMax Hailuo 2.3 Fast · image to video
  5. EDIT

    Cut to the kick drum

    The edit is code. Cuts and a subtle pulse follow every kick drum hit pulled from the track, the lyrics pop in word by word, and each "woof woof" gets a stamp. The same timeline renders both the widescreen and vertical cuts, with the vertical crop following Archie shot by shot.

    Remotion · React + TypeScript
